preamble: Regressive place assimilation of the bilabial nasal [m] to the velar nasal [ŋ] before a following velar consonant ([k], [ɡ]). It is categorical in some sandhi systems (Sanskrit sam- + velar, Latin com- + velar) and gradient in connected English speech, where corpus data show that labial nasals assimilate less often than alveolar /n/ but do assimilate.

examples.note: Optional assimilation of word-final /m/ to a following velar in fast speech; Coleman, Renwick & Temple (2016) found statistical evidence of labial-nasal place assimilation in the Audio British National Corpus, previously reported only anecdotally.
The prefix com- surfaces with a velar nasal before c/g (written n), cf. also congregō 'gather together'; it keeps [m] before labials (compōnō, combūrō).
Final -m of a prefix or word before a stop becomes anusvāra or the homorganic nasal of the following stop's class, here velar [ŋ] (also written saṅkalpa).

sources: Coleman, J., Renwick, M. E. L., & Temple, R. A. M. (2016). Probabilistic underspecification in nasal place assimilation. Phonology 33(3), 425–458. https://doi.org/10.1017/S0952675716000208
